bug: A key-to-single-job shortcut drops retained attempts; key traversal changes ordering; a shared project/kind filter bug returns jobs outside the requested scope.
oracle: Literal expected sequences of first.id, second.id and retried.id, with explicit empty export-kind result and active/history/since results. No call to list computes an expectation.
seam: JobQueue.submit/cancel/retry/list public methods, consumed by HTTP jobs routes and DerivativeService.status; only Date is controlled to make timestamp ties deterministic.
refactor: Any index or scan implementation can replace the queue internals while returning the same caller-visible IDs and ordering. No private fields, call counts or source strings asserted.
unique: The existing detached/external-source case has one internal attempt per key; retry/cancellation tests do not query retained keyed history or filter composition. This is the lowest stable owner of these list results.
reason: The incoming test used list(filter).filter(...) as its own expected value, allowing common filter bugs to pass. Replace that oracle with seven small literal result cases, use a contrasting kind, remove the unsupported not-a-date vector, and fake only Date.

test: keeps key lookups identical to full listing after journal replacement, duplicate-key recovery and pruning
survivingTest: restores keyed journal history in stable order and drops pruned keys from lookups
contract: Valid journal recovery preserves all retained jobs under repeated keys and existing insertion order; terminal jobs older than seven days beyond the newest 500 disappear from memory and keyed lookups.
source: S04 JB-030 and CA-020 persistence/retention contracts; docs/wp-notes/perf-hunt-engine.md explicitly preserves journal replacement, duplicate-key history and equal-timestamp ordering.
bug: Journal replay resets insertion ordinals and reorders existing jobs, or pruning leaves indexed IDs whose entries no longer exist, crashing subsequent caller lookups.
oracle: Literal restored ID order [first, other, duplicate], then exactly four removed jobs from 504 valid terminal records under the documented 500-job retention floor; old keys return [] and job_finished_500 remains.
seam: JobQueue constructor/start/cancel/wait/prune/list plus the documented jobs.jsonl wire format, with a supplied clock. No internal index or insertion counter is inspected.
refactor: A new data structure or journal reader passes if valid serialized jobs recover in the same observable order and pruned jobs are no longer returned. Fixture chronology and expected IDs are independent of queue algorithms.
unique: Existing crash-recovery tests do not combine pre-start replacement with duplicate-key history. cache.test.ts checks ordinary prune retention, but never keyed lookup after removal; it cannot catch stale index references.
reason: Replace the queue-as-own-oracle comparisons with explicit IDs. Two pre-start entries make replacement-order bugs observable. Seed 501 fresh valid completed journal records in one write instead of 501 submit/fail/journal cycles, then advance the clock eight days and prune.
